authored, delivered, protected, or materially advanced a concrete governmental action, resource, program, policy, or benefit.","clarification":"Classify a release as credit-claiming when it explicitly links the senator's action to a tangible result. This includes claiming to have secured federal funds or grants; authored, introduced, or successfully passed legislation; obtained an agency decision; negotiated an agreement; or protected a local institution, project, or benefit. A claim may be individual or shared with other legislators. Announcements of an accomplishment count when the text attributes a meaningful role in producing it to the senator.","positive_examples":[{"document_id":"1862","explanation":"Baucus and Tester explicitly state that they delivered $12.5 million for Butte military projects and describe their role in obtaining it."},{"document_id":"2318","explanation":"Durbin says he helped secure an expedited federal review and returned the South Suburban Airport project to the priority list for federal funding."},{"document_id":"1257","explanation":"DeWine connects a local fire grant to the FIRE Act that he wrote and passed, claiming both legislative authorship and a resulting benefit."}],"negative_clarification":"Do not classify as credit-claiming when the senator merely states a policy position, criticizes or praises another actor, explains a vote, urges future action, attends a hearing or meeting, honors someone, or announces agency funding without taking credit for obtaining it.
